rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for animal or body fat and the default choice.

example.english: This fat is energy stored by the body.
example.traditional: 呢啲脂肪係身體儲起嚟嘅能量。
example.jyutping: ni1 di1 zi1 fong1 hai6 san1 tai2 cyu5 hei2 lei4 ge3 nang4 loeng6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a person or animal carrying excess body fat.

example.english: You seem to have gotten fat lately.
example.jyutping: nei5 gan6 paai4 hou2 ci5 fei4 zo2 wo3

rows.note: Use this for food that is greasy or has too much oil.

example.english: This dish is too fat for me, so I’m not eating it.
example.traditional: 呢碟餸太油喇，我唔食喇。
example.jyutping: ni1 dip6 sung3 taai3 jau4 laa3 ngo5 m4 sik6 laa3

rows.note: Use this for an object that is unusually thick or bulky, such as a wallet.

example.english: This wallet is too fat to fit in my trouser pocket.
example.traditional: 呢個銀包厚身，擺唔落條褲袋。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 ngan4 baau1 hau5 san1 baai2 m4 lok6 tiu4 fu3 doi6

rows.note: Use this for excess or wasteful elements in an organization, especially in formal descriptions.

example.english: The reorganization is meant to remove fat from the organization.
example.traditional: 公司重組係為咗清除冗餘部門。
example.jyutping: gung1 si1 cung4 zou2 hai6 wai6 zo2 cing1 ceoi4 jung2 jyu4 bou6 mun4

rows.note: Use this when the organizational fat specifically means redundant employees or staff.

example.english: The company will lay off some redundant staff to trim the organizational fat.
example.traditional: 公司今年會裁減一批冗員。
example.jyutping: gung1 si1 gam1 nin4 wui5 coi4 gaam2 jat1 pai1 jung2 jyun4
